newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian opposition asks West to pressure Berisha.
newsitem.headline: Albanian opposition asks West to pressure Berisha.

text.p: Albania's Forum for Democracy opposition alliance appealed to the West on Wednesday to put pressure on President Sali Berisha to end emergency rule and find a political solution to avoid civil war.

The Forum asked for help from the United States, European Union and international organisations a day after talks between its main component, the Socialist Party, and Berisha failed to make progress towards political compromise.
"Being convinced that the crisis has a political solution, we appeal to them to do their best to avoid a civil war in Albania," the Forum said in a written statement.
The alliance urged the West to "use all their influence on the Albanian government and president Berisha to put an end to the state of emergency and start a real dialogue with the opposition".

It also asked the European Union to send a delegation to Tirana and said Western financial aid should be linked to a political solution. European and U.S. observers, it said, should keep watch on progress in monitoring human rights.
At least 20 people have died in violence in southern Albania since last week and troops were trying to quell the unrest opn Wednesday.
The Forum was founded in January after the outbreak of violent protests by investors who had lost life savings in the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes.

It brought together for the first time a disparate grouping of parties of both left and right, plus former political prisoners, all saying they were committed to a peaceful change in government. But it lacks leaders with mass appeal and has few economic experts.
The Forum has proposed the formation of a government of technocrats to haul Albania out of its economic crisis.

But Berisha told Socialist leaders at Tuesday's talks he opposed any coalition with their party and said his earlier attempts at compromise had been interpreted as a sign of weakness, leading to the latest violence.
